section_summary: This section (pages 48-123) of decimal file 894.017 covers diplomatic correspondence, intelligence reports, and legal analyses from August to September 1948 concerning the revision of Japan's National Public Service Law and the promulgation of Cabinet Ordinance No. 201, which prohibited strikes and collective bargaining by government employees following General Douglas MacArthur's letter of July 22, 1948. It includes protests from Soviet representatives in Tokyo and Washington asserting that the anti-strike restrictions violate the Potsdam Declaration and Far Eastern Commission policies, as well as General MacArthur's and the State Department's firm rebuttals. In addition, the documents capture internal Japanese political reactions and legal justifications by the Ashida Cabinet and Attorney General Yoshio Suzuki, assessments of communist influence within labor unions, British and Australian diplomatic representations, and recommendations from the U.S. Department of Labor.

subfiles.about: Transmits a newspaper editorial analyzing the political prospects of Prime Minister Ashida's Democratic Party in connection with the upcoming Diet revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: A Nippon Times editorial argues that postponing elections to revise the public service law helps the Democratic Party restore political strength.
subfiles.title: The Nippon Times: The Democrats' New Lease on Life (Enclosure No. 4 to Despatch No. 514)

subfiles.about: Transmits an English translation of a letter from Major-General A. P. Kislenko to General MacArthur demanding the revocation of orders restricting Japanese public workers' labor rights.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Acting Political Adviser forwards Soviet member Kislenko's letter demanding cancellation of MacArthur's July 22 directives and Osaka police regulations as violations of the Potsdam Declaration.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 527: Soviet Statement Concerning Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Transmits an interview with moderate labor leaders and reports views of Bank of Japan Governor Ichimada and Tokyo University President Nambara on public service revisions and communist influence.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards a memorandum of conversation with three moderate labor leaders from the Democratic League of NCIU who express deep concern that banning collective bargaining harms the labor movement, while acknowledging communist excesses prompted Occupation intervention. Bank of Japan Governor Hisato Ichimada and Tokyo University President Shigeru Nambara endorse MacArthur's move as a necessary check on communist subversion, though Nambara notes James S. Killen's resignation revealed the Occupation as Japan's true ruler. The file includes duplicate ozalid copies of both the despatch and the enclosed memorandum.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 531: Opinions of Japanese Leaders Concerning Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Communicates the British Government's concerns that Cabinet Ordinance No. 201 excessively deprives Japanese industrial and enterprise workers of collective bargaining and strike rights.
subfiles.from: Department of State, Washington (George C. Marshall)
subfiles.summary: The State Department relays British representations arguing that railway and monopoly workers should retain normal union rights and regular civil servants should have arbitration machinery.
subfiles.title: Outgoing Telegram No. 308: British Government Comments on Japanese Government Ordinance Regarding Rights of Public Employees
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-references Tokyo Airgram A-182 of September 4, 1948 regarding Labor Minister Kanju Kato's reaction to the public service law, filed under decimal 894.002.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet for Tokyo Airgram A-182 regarding Labor Minister Kanju Kato's reaction to civil service revision, filed under 894.002.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Airgram A-182 Concerning Reaction of Labor Minister Kato Kanju

subfiles.about: Reports on SCAP Government Section's drafting of the National Public Service Law revision bill and ministerial preparations for Diet consideration.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports that SCAP Government Section prepared the public service revision bill, while a five-minister Cabinet committee finalized details for submission to the National Diet.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-185: Revision of the National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Reports on petitions from major Japanese labor unions presented to the Allied Council protesting the revision of the National Public Service Law.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports petitions from railway, communications, and teachers' unions protesting public service law revisions, identifying them as part of a Communist Party anti-Occupation campaign.
subfiles.title: Airgram: Petitions Protesting Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Provides an informal, confidential report on Blaine Hoover's civil service program, Patrick Shaw's meeting with General MacArthur, and Allied Council deliberations.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald reports Blaine Hoover's efforts to create an American-style civil service, discussions with British and Australian representatives, and MacArthur's strategy during the August 28 Allied Council meeting.
subfiles.title: Personal Letter from William J. Sebald to John M. Allison Regarding Civil Service Reform
subfiles.to: John M. Allison, Chief, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs, Department of State, Washington

subfiles.about: Transmits recommendations of the Labor Department's Trade Union Advisory Committee urging protection of Japanese government workers' rights and restoration of abrogated labor contracts.
subfiles.from: John W. Gibson, Acting Secretary of Labor, Washington
subfiles.summary: Acting Secretary Gibson conveys union advisory committee recommendations calling on defense and state departments to restore abrogated contracts and preserve trade union rights for Japanese public workers.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary of Labor John W. Gibson Regarding Labor Relations of Japanese Government Employees

subfiles.about: Transmits English translations and Japanese originals of official government statements, ministerial notices, and legal opinions upholding the validity and enforcement of Cabinet Ordinance No. 201.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch 616 transmits English translations and Japanese texts of official announcements by Personnel Commission Chairman Kiyoshi Asai, Chief Cabinet Secretary Gizo Tomabechi, and Attorney General Yoshio Suzuki regarding Cabinet Ordinance No. 201. Government directives outline strict prohibitions on strikes, collective bargaining, and full-time union positions, while maintaining existing health, retirement, and welfare benefits for civil servants. An extensive legal opinion by Attorney General Suzuki defends the constitutionality of Cabinet Ordinance No. 201 under Imperial Ordinance No. 542, asserting that SCAP directives implement Japan's Potsdam surrender commitments without violating legislative prerogatives under the new Constitution.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 616: Official Statements Concerning Revision of National Public Service Law

subfiles.about: Transmits a public statement by General MacArthur repudiating Soviet criticisms of Occupation labor policies and denouncing Soviet detention of Japanese prisoners of war.
subfiles.from: William J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards General MacArthur's press release dismissing Soviet Ambassador Panyushkin's charges as baseless, warning against communist destruction of Japanese trade unionism, and condemning Soviet retention of Japanese prisoners of war.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 623: General MacArthur's Reply to Charges by Ambassador Panyushkin on the Rights of Government Workers

subfiles.about: Instructs the U.S. Member on the Far Eastern Commission to oppose a Soviet policy proposal on Japanese government workers and press for an immediate vote.
subfiles.from: Charles E. Saltzman, Assistant Secretary of State, Washington
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Saltzman instructs the U.S. Member on the Far Eastern Commission to reject the Soviet proposal on Japanese government workers (FEC-318) and bring it to a prompt vote.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Policy on Japanese Government Workers (FEC-318)
subfiles.to: United States Member, Far Eastern Commission (Frank R. McCoy)
